title: Onboarding gates and runtime signature checklist for ephemeral model forks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Clarify minimum runtime and acceptance checks for ingesting ephemeral forks (community-derived model variants) into the model catalog. The goal is to create a lightweight but rigorous gating surface that prevents runtime incompatibilities and high-cost regressions while keeping onboarding friction low for exploratory community submissions.
scope_changes: IN: define ABI-style runtime signature (tokenizer hash + model-config subset + operator surface) as a required metadata field for ephemeral forks
IN: automated compatibility validator that runs a small suite of behavioral smoke tests and a runtime resource sanity check on a single GPU profile
OUT: full eval suite for initial admission (we will run full evals after staged admission),
OUT: mandatory hard pinning to an internal 'production' variant for ephemeral forks — instead we allow soft-pin with explicit fallback mapping
decisions: Require an explicit 'compat_fingerprint' metadata blob: tokenizer_digest, architecture_tag, kv_cache_dims, and opset_hash
Admit ephemeral forks into a 'quarantine' catalog channel that defaults to a lower SLA and cost-tier
Allow soft-pinning (unpinned by default) but require a declared fallback target that is runtime-compatible
Validator must enforce memory and peak-allocation thresholds for the declared serving settings (sequence_length, batch_size) before admission
tradeoffs: Stricter ingest checks reduce operator burden but increase initial friction for contributors
Lightweight behavioral tests may miss edge-case failures; mitigated by staged rollout and automated regression monitoring
Quarantining reduces user surprise when a model degrades but increases catalog complexity and UI surface for consumers
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable compat_fingerprint spec published in the catalog docs and validated by the ingest CLI
Automated validator runs on CI: given a candidate model and declared serving profile it reports PASS/FAIL with actionable diagnostics
Runtime smoke tests (3 scenarios: short chat, long-context generation, embed-only) pass on the smallest recommended GPU with latency within SLO and peak memory within threshold
Fallback mapping populated or admission blocked: each ephemeral fork must list at least one compatible fallback variant key
Catalog UI surfaces 'quarantine' badge and cost tier for admitted ephemeral forks
Rollout plan executed: first 10 admitted forks monitored for 2 weeks with alerts for quality regressions tied to prompt set A
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): internal-only admission of up to 5 ephemeral forks; validate validator outputs and UI flags
Phase 2 (4 weeks): open beta to community contributors; require contributors to add compat_fingerprint and fallback mapping
Phase 3: promote well-behaved forks to 'catalog-preview' channel and enable auto-scaling suggestions
test_plan: Unit tests for compat_fingerprint parsing and opset_hash verification
Integration test: ingest -> validator -> quarantine flag set -> UI shows badge
Performance test: run long-context scenario (4k tokens) and verify KV cache shape matches declared kv_cache_dims
Behavioral smoke: run 20 prompt variants from PromptSet-A and assert top-1 non-toxic response rate and embed cosine stability
Canary rollback: simulate a failed admission and assert runtime routing falls back to declared fallback variant
implementation_notes: ENG: extend model-metadata schema with compat_fingerprint and fallback_variant fields
ENG: add a new ingest validator microservice with pluggable checks and a human-review flag
PM: update onboarding docs and create a contributor quickstart for ephemeral forks
DX: add 'quarantine' filter and badge to catalog UI, and expose fallback mapping in variant detail panel
next_steps: PM to finalize compat_fingerprint spec with runtime team by 2026-03-16
ENG to prototype validator and run against 10 community forks (ENG-1842 owner)
Design to mock catalog UI badge and quarantine UX (deliverables: figma link)
Schedule security review if validator will execute arbitrary model binaries (security_review_required=true)
